subject: SIG: Clarification on Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment evidence
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-corp.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up — need precise distinctions for deployment modes

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the initial SIG spreadsheet. We're finishing our vendor review and need a clear, concise mapping of which controls and evidence apply to Redwood's Hosted, Dedicated (reserved), and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. In particular:

- Data residency / region guarantees for each mode
- Who manages the KMS keys and where they are stored
- Network boundaries and whether customer VPN/VPC peering is required for Private
- Which SOC 2 evidence items (logs, access reviews, config screenshots) differ between modes

Could you attach a short one-page matrix and any sample artifacts we can include in our packet? If possible, we'd like a brief explanation we can include in our SIG question comments (for the assessor) that explains the operational differences.

We can do a 30-minute call Tuesday if that helps.

Thanks — Laura
Security Operations
Acme Corp

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, rohan.mehta@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — need precise distinctions for deployment modes

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a short matrix and preliminary evidence pointers; below is a succinct mapping you can paste into the SIG comment fields.

Attachment: redwood_SIG_deployment_matrix.pdf (application/pdf) — 1-page matrix with controls mapping
Attachment: redwood_data_flow_vpc.png (image/png) — VPC/on-prem data flow diagram
Attachment: redwood_sig_responses_20250312.xlsx (spreadsheet) — answers keyed to your SIG IDs

Quick pasteable text for the SIG question comment (editable):
"Redwood Inference supports three deployment modes with consistent API and security controls; differences are noted by where customer data is stored and who manages infrastructure keys.

- Hosted: Redwood-managed infrastructure in our regional cloud clusters. Customer data is logically isolated; encryption-at-rest keys are managed by Redwood KMS integrated with our HSM. Regional placement can be selected from our offered regions (US, EU). SOC 2 evidence: hosted cluster config screenshots, centralized audit logs, key management screenshots.

- Dedicated (Reserved): Dedicated GPU pools provisioned for a single customer within Redwood's control plane. Data separation is enforced at the tenant layer; Redwood manages underlying keys by default, but we offer customer-managed KMS option for an additional compliance contract. SOC 2 evidence: dedicated cluster allocation records, tenant access reviews, encryption key ownership documentation.

- Private (VPC / on-prem): Control plane can be customer-hosted or Redwood-managed with customer VPC peering; customer controls network boundary. Customers own KMS keys (BYOK) when on-prem or VPC-hosted. SOC 2 evidence: network peering configs, customer KMS attestations, on-prem deployment runbooks, and audit log exports under customer tenancy.

If you want, we can mark specific SIG question IDs with the exact artifact file names included in the attachments.

Next steps: I'll assign Monica to prepare the SOC 2 artifact list for the Hosted and Dedicated modes and Rohan will prepare the technical notes for VPC/on-prem and the BYOK flow. Are you available Tues 10:30 AM PT for a 30-min sync?

— Jasmine
Senior Account Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-corp.com>

Jasmine — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups from our assessor:

1) For Hosted, can you confirm whether Redwood's HSM is a cloud provider-managed HSM or a customer-dedicated HSM? We need exact vendor/managed details for the SIG fields.
2) For Dedicated: is there a documented option and pricing for customer-managed KMS? We will flag that as a requirement for our procurement team if it's available.
3) For Private (VPC/on-prem): who owns the audit log retention policy — Redwood's default or the customer's? Our default requirement is 365 days for all logs retained in our control plane.

Also the assessor asked for a sample audit log export (redacted) — if you can provide an example file name and the fields we can expect, that will speed their review.

We can do the 10:30 AM PT sync today — I just invited the assessor to the call.

Laura

From: monica.patel@redwood.com
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, rohan.mehta@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Mar 2025 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — need precise distinctions for deployment modes

Hi Laura — rapid answers below, and I've uploaded the sample artifacts to the Drive folder linked in the SIG spreadsheet.

1) Hosted HSM: Redwood's Hosted deployments use cloud-provider HSMs (AWS KMS with AWS CloudHSM-backed keys in our US regions). We maintain the HSM cluster for Hosted; keys are managed by Redwood KMS unless you choose BYOK via Dedicated or Private.

2) Dedicated KMS (customer-managed): Yes — we offer a customer-managed KMS option for Dedicated deployments. It's documented in the Dedicated onboarding addendum (pricing and minimum commit apply). Contact your SE for an estimate; I attached the onboarding addendum excerpt as a file reference in the Drive folder.

3) Audit log retention for Private (VPC/on-prem): When the control plane is customer-hosted, the customer configures retention. For Redwood-managed Private with VPC peering, we default to 90 days but can extend to 365 days under an enterprise SLA (we can include an addendum).

Sample audit export: redwood_audit_export_sample_20240228.csv — fields: timestamp, user.email, user.id, action, resource.type, resource.id, source.ip, request_id, result, latency_ms. The CSV is redacted to remove customer identifiers and is in the Drive folder.

I also attached a short KB snippet describing the BYOK flow for VPC and on-prem PKI exchanges.

Let us know if the assessor needs screenshots of the KMS UI or the HSM vendor confirmation letter — we can provide both.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Sr. Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference
